APPRENTICESHIP AGREEMENT — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Acme Trade Program

APPRENTICE AGREEMENT DECLARATION
Apprentice: Jordan Alex Lee
Employer or program sponsor: Acme Trade Program
Trade, craft, or occupation: Electrician
Apprenticeship term: 4 years
Graduated wage schedule: 50% of journey-level wage in year 1, increasing 10% annually

The following statements describe this apprenticeship as structured by Acme Trade Program. They are factual statements about this specific arrangement, not a legal conclusion about whether it satisfies California Labor Code Chapter 4's requirements for an apprentice agreement.

Approval and filing: ☐ This apprentice agreement has been approved by a local joint apprenticeship committee, by the parties to a collective bargaining agreement, or by the administrator, with a copy filed with the Division of Apprenticeship Standards ☐ Approval and filing have not yet occurred

Instruction measurement approach: ☐ Time-based (at least 144 hours of related and supplemental instruction and 2,000 hours of on-the-job learning) ☐ Competency-based ☐ Hybrid ☐ Not yet determined

Probationary period: the first 6 months (not to exceed the shorter of 25 percent of the apprenticeship term or one year)

Related and supplemental instruction provider: _______________________________________________

DEFINITION OF "APPRENTICE"
California Labor Code Chapter 4 defines an “apprentice,” for purposes of that chapter, as a person at least 16 years of age who has entered into a written apprentice agreement with an employer or a program sponsor. The statute names the employer or program sponsor — not a joint apprenticeship committee — as the counterparty to that written agreement; a joint apprenticeship committee's role, described elsewhere in this chapter, is to help establish, administer, and approve apprenticeship programs and agreements, not to be the party who signs the agreement with the apprentice.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "The term “apprentice” as used in this chapter, means a person at least 16 years of age who has entered into a written agreement, in this chapter called an “apprentice agreement,” with an employer or program sponsor."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3077 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3077.)
  Known gap: This is a single California statutory section (Cal. Labor Code § 3077); no additional independent source was found for the definition itself. The 16-year minimum age and the written-agreement requirement stated here define “apprentice” only for purposes of this specific chapter of California's Labor Code — a different statute, a different state's law, or a federal Registered Apprenticeship program could define the term differently, and this document does not identify which definition, if any, applies outside California's own statutory apprenticeship scheme. This document is informational only: it does not itself determine that any specific individual qualifies as an apprentice under this chapter, and does not determine that any specific written agreement is, or is not, a valid apprentice agreement.

REQUIRED CONTENT OF AN APPRENTICE AGREEMENT
California Labor Code § 3078 requires that every apprentice agreement made under this chapter contain, directly or by reference: the names of the contracting parties; the apprentice's date of birth; a statement of the trade, craft, or business to be taught and when the apprenticeship begins and ends; a statement of the hours to be spent in work and the learning objectives for related and supplemental instruction (subject to a combined weekly-hours cap tied to the apprentice's age); a schedule of the trade processes to be taught and the approximate time for each; a statement of the graduated wage scale and whether required school time is compensated; a probationary-period provision; a provision routing unresolved disputes to the administrator; a provision allowing an employer who cannot continue to transfer the agreement to another employer with the administrator's approval and the apprentice's consent; any additional terms prescribed by the California Apprenticeship Council or the Chief of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards; and a clause addressing liability for an injury sustained during school work after employment has ended. This list is more extensive than a shorter list built only around parties, trade, term, wages, hours, and a probationary period — the statute requires several additional specific items, including the apprentice's date of birth and a process-by-process training schedule.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "Every apprentice agreement entered into under this chapter shall directly, or by reference, contain: (a) The names of the contracting parties. (b) The date of birth of the apprentice. (c) A statement of the trade, craft, or business which the apprentice is to be taught, and the time at which the apprenticeship will begin and end. (d) A statement showing the number of hours to be spent by the apprentice in work and the learning objectives to be accomplished through related and supplemental instruction, except as otherwise provided under Section 3074."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3078 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3078.)
  "(e) A statement setting forth a schedule of the processes in the trade or industry divisions in which the apprentice is to be taught and the approximate time to be spent at each process. (f) A statement of the graduated scale of wages to be paid the apprentice and whether the required schooltime shall be compensated. (g) A statement providing for a period of probation during which time the apprentice agreement may be terminated by the program sponsor at the request in writing of either party, and providing that after the probationary period the apprentice agreement may be terminated by the administrator by mutual agreement of all parties thereto, or canceled by the administrator for good and sufficient reason."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3078 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3078.)
  Known gap: Both citations below quote different subdivisions of the same statutory section, Cal. Labor Code § 3078, and are treated as one source, not independent. This document is informational only: it does not itself draft, complete, or file any apprentice agreement, and does not determine that any specific document satisfies § 3078's content requirements. This is California's own statutory list for its own apprenticeship framework; whether, and what, an equivalent list requires under any other state's apprenticeship law is not addressed here.

APPROVAL OF AN APPRENTICE AGREEMENT
An apprentice agreement made under this chapter must be approved — by the local joint apprenticeship committee, or by the parties to a collective bargaining agreement, or, where neither exists, by the administrator — and a copy of the approved agreement must be filed with the Division of Apprenticeship Standards. Separately, the term of apprenticeship for each apprenticeable occupation is itself approved by the Chief of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards, applying the standards set out at Labor Code § 3078.5. Approval, in other words, is not a single event performed only by the Division or its Chief directly on every agreement: the immediate approving body is ordinarily the joint committee, the collective-bargaining parties, or the administrator, with the Division receiving a filed copy and the Chief separately approving the occupation's term.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "Every apprentice agreement under this chapter shall be approved by the local joint apprenticeship committee or the parties to a collective bargaining agreement, or by the administrator where there is no collective bargaining agreement or joint committee, a copy of which shall be filed with the Division of Apprenticeship Standards."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3079 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3079.)
  "The term of apprenticeship for each apprenticeable occupation shall be approved by the chief in accordance with the standards set forth in Section 3078.5."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3077 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3077.)
  Known gap: The two citations below are drawn from two independently enacted sections, Cal. Labor Code §§ 3077 and 3079, not subsections of one section. Neither section quoted here states, in so many words, what legal consequence follows for an apprentice agreement that was never approved or never filed with the Division — this document does not assume, and the statutory text located does not itself say, that an unapproved agreement is void or unenforceable as a general matter; that specific consequence is not resolved by the statutory text found and is left as an open point. This document is informational only: it does not itself approve, execute, or file any apprentice agreement with any committee, administrator, or the Division of Apprenticeship Standards, and does not determine that any specific agreement has been, or will be, approved.

WAGE SCHEDULE FOR APPRENTICES
Every apprentice agreement made under this chapter must contain a statement of the graduated scale of wages to be paid the apprentice and whether required school time is compensated — the statute requires the agreement to state a graduated wage scale, but its own text does not itself set out specific percentages of a journey-level wage or a specific schedule of increases. Those figures are instead set at the program-standards level: for programs in the building and construction trades and for firefighter occupations, the California Apprenticeship Council issues rules and regulations establishing minimum-wage, maximum-hours, and working-condition standards (no lower than this chapter's own floor); for other programs, an equivalent standard-setting role is assigned to the Chief of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards, and a joint apprenticeship committee with delegated written authority is assigned the function of establishing wage rates in accordance with whichever of those two standards applies to its program.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "A statement of the graduated scale of wages to be paid the apprentice and whether the required schooltime shall be compensated."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3078 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3078.)
  "The council shall issue rules and regulations which establish standards for minimum wages, maximum hours, and working conditions for apprentice agreements in the building and construction trades and for firefighter occupations, hereinafter in this chapter referred to as apprenticeship standards, which in no case shall be lower than those prescribed by this chapter"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3071 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3071.)
  "The function of a joint apprenticeship committee, when specific written authority is delegated by the parent organizations represented, shall be to establish work processes, wage rates, working conditions for apprentices, the number of apprentices which shall be employed in the trade under apprentice agreements, and aid in the adjustment of apprenticeship disputes in accordance with standards for apprenticeship set up by the California Apprenticeship Council for programs in the building and construction trades and for firefighters or by the Chief of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards for other programs."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3076 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3076.)
  Known gap: The three citations below are drawn from three independently enacted sections of the same chapter — Cal. Labor Code §§ 3078(f), 3071, and 3076 — not subsections of one section. Section 3071's own quoted text expressly scopes the California Apprenticeship Council's wage-standards authority to programs in the building and construction trades and for firefighter occupations; § 3076 (quoted for the Chief's parallel role for "other programs") does not itself spell out that Chief-set wage-standard-setting process in the same regulatory detail as § 3071 does for the Council, and this document does not independently verify the content of any specific program's wage schedule or regulations issued under either section. This document is informational only: it does not itself state, calculate, or verify the graduated wage schedule, percentage, or rate that applies to any specific apprentice or program.

RELATED AND SUPPLEMENTAL INSTRUCTION REQUIREMENT
An apprentice agreement must state the number of hours the apprentice will spend in work and the learning objectives to be met through related and supplemental instruction, and the combined weekly hours of work and required instruction may not exceed the maximum hours of work the law otherwise prescribes for a person of the apprentice's age. Where a program measures its apprenticeship term using the time-based approach — the approach that programs in the building and construction trades and for firefighter occupations must use — the statute itself specifies a minimum: at least 144 hours of related and supplemental instruction and 2,000 hours of on-the-job learning, as described in a work process schedule. A program outside those two categories is not required to use the time-based approach, however; it may instead measure the term using a competency-based or hybrid approach, each of which the statute defines by a minimum on-the-job-learning period of at least six months rather than by a fixed related-and-supplemental-instruction hour count.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "A statement showing the number of hours to be spent by the apprentice in work and the learning objectives to be accomplished through related and supplemental instruction, except as otherwise provided under Section 3074. In no case shall the combined weekly hours of work and required related and supplemental instruction of the apprentice exceed the maximum number of hours of work prescribed by law for a person of the age of the apprentice."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3078 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3078.)
  "The time-based approach measures skill acquisition through the individual apprentice’s completion of at least 144 hours of related and supplemental instruction and 2,000 hours of on-the-job learning as described in a work process schedule."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3078.5 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3078.5.)
  Known gap: The two citations below are drawn from two independently enacted sections, Cal. Labor Code §§ 3078(d) and 3078.5, not subsections of one section. The 144-hour and 2,000-hour figures quoted below apply specifically to programs using the time-based approach to measuring the apprenticeship term; this document does not determine which measurement approach — time-based, competency-based, or hybrid — any specific program outside the building and construction trades or firefighter occupations has adopted, and does not calculate the specific related-and-supplemental-instruction hours that would apply under a competency-based or hybrid program. This document is informational only: it does not itself schedule, track, or verify the instruction or on-the-job hours completed by any specific apprentice.

TERMINATION AND CANCELLATION OF AN APPRENTICE AGREEMENT
Every apprentice agreement must provide for a probationary period during which the program sponsor may terminate the agreement at the written request of either party; the statute caps that probationary period at whichever is shorter — 25 percent of the length of the program or one year — with full credit given toward completion of the apprenticeship for time already served during probation. After the probationary period, the statute allows the agreement to be terminated by the administrator by mutual agreement of all parties, or canceled by the administrator for good and sufficient reason. Separately, the administrator may investigate — on the complaint of any interested person, or on the administrator's own initiative — whether there has been a violation of an apprentice agreement's terms, and must give the parties a fair and impartial hearing after reasonable notice before making a determination; that determination can itself be appealed, and no lawsuit to enforce an apprentice agreement or recover damages for its breach may be filed until this chapter's administrative remedies have been exhausted.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-02]
  "A statement providing for a period of probation during which time the apprentice agreement may be terminated by the program sponsor at the request in writing of either party, and providing that after the probationary period the apprentice agreement may be terminated by the administrator by mutual agreement of all parties thereto, or canceled by the administrator for good and sufficient reason. The period of probation shall be reasonable in relation to the full apprenticeship term, with full credit given for such period toward completion of the apprenticeship, and in no event shall exceed the shorter of 25 percent of the length of the program or one year."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3078 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3078.)
  "Upon the complaint of any interested person or upon his or her own initiative, the administrator may investigate to determine if there has been a violation of the terms of an apprentice agreement, made under this chapter, and he or she may hold hearings, inquiries, and other proceedings necessary to such investigations and determinations."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3081 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3081.)
  Known gap: The two citations below are drawn from two independently enacted provisions, Cal. Labor Code § 3078(g) and § 3081, not subsections of one section. The statutory text located requires the original apprentice agreement to be approved with a copy filed with the Division of Apprenticeship Standards at the outset (§ 3079, addressed in a separate clause in this document), but this document did not locate statutory text imposing a separate, independent notice-to-the-Division requirement specifically triggered by a later termination or cancellation, as distinct from the administrator's and Division's general administrative role in the agreement — that is disclosed here as a genuine gap in what was found in the statutory text, not as an affirmative statement that no such requirement exists anywhere in this chapter's implementing regulations. This document is informational only: it does not itself terminate, cancel, investigate, or adjudicate any specific apprentice agreement, and does not determine that any specific ground for termination or cancellation exists in any specific case.

Jordan Alex Lee and Acme Trade Program each acknowledge that they have reviewed the apprentice agreement declaration above and this information sheet's description of the California statutory requirements that can apply to apprentice agreements under Labor Code Chapter 4.

The statutory text located requires the original apprentice agreement to be approved with a copy filed with the Division of Apprenticeship Standards at the outset (§ 3079, addressed in a separate clause in this document), but this document did not locate statutory text imposing a separate, independent notice-to-the-Division requirement specifically triggered by a later termination or cancellation, as distinct from the administrator's and Division's general administrative role in the agreement — that is disclosed here as a genuine gap in what was found in the statutory text, not as an affirmative statement that no such requirement exists anywhere in this chapter's implementing regulations. This document is informational only: it does not itself terminate, cancel, investigate, or adjudicate any specific apprentice agreement, and does not determine that any specific ground for termination or cancellation exists in any specific case.
